title: The affordance surface offers deployment.set_target, so the binding control has something to spend
description:
PRODUCER ROW filed by architect-fa3a3e17 on 2026-09-06 at governor-afbde490's 13:50Z direction (the "no target-binding UI" gap in worker-f72a1438's audit of task-84cd2e55aae942cf8d56657308215fde).

THE GAP IS THE OFFER, NOT THE CONTROL - and the card already says so in its own source. `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goal-deployments.tsx:189-192`:
  // set_target affordance is offered, so a control here would have none to spend.
  `Bind a target for ${view.environment} first, with deployment.set_target.`
  + " This screen cannot bind one yet, so it has to be bound outside the"
and `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/deploy-port.ts:29` records the same measurement: "excluding tests returns zero. So a `deployment.set_target` dispatch has no affordance to [spend]".
So the browser is not missing a button by oversight - it is correctly refusing to render a control that would have no affordance to spend. THE PRODUCER IS THE MISSING PIECE, and this row is it.

THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS task-2cedb26a598540bd9bab17046592a7bb (the `deployment.deploy` per-goal offer, planned 2026-09-06). Read that row's plan first and follow it: the same generic emission at affordance-read.ts:282-284, the same `aggregateIdFor` fallthrough in bootstrap-sequence.ts that targets the PROJECT, and the same requirement to assert the target id BY VALUE against what the card matches.

THE GRANULARITY DIFFERS FROM THE DEPLOY OFFER, AND THAT IS THE DECISION THIS ROW MUST MAKE. `deployment.set_target`'s payload keys are `["environment", "network", "sshTarget", "url"]` (daemon-command-payload-keys.ts:165) and the durable target is keyed `deploy-target:<projectId>:<environment>` (deploy-target-contracts.ts:84) - so unlike `deployment.deploy`, whose environment is chosen at dispatch from a single goal-scoped offer, BINDING is a per-(project, environment) act. Decide whether the offer is goal-scoped with the environment in the payload, or one per environment, and state it in a comment at the offer site the way task-2cedb26a requires. Do not leave the browser to infer it.

WITHHOLDING IS THE INVERSE OF THE DEPLOY OFFER'S. A deploy offer is withheld when NO target is bound; a set_target offer is what an operator needs precisely THEN. Say what the rule is - it is not "withheld when already bound", because rebinding is legitimate.

NOT IN SCOPE: the binding control itself (the parent task-84cd2e55 owns the card), the deploy offer (task-2cedb26a), and how set_target executes (task-358b6ec8).
definitionOfDone: The affordance read offers `deployment.set_target`, targeted at the aggregate the consuming control will match, asserted BY VALUE on `targetAggregateId` against the production surface read - not a hand-built frame. `git grep -c "set_target" -- apps/control-room/src` excluding tests currently proves zero affordance to spend; that count must become nonzero through a real offer.

THE GRANULARITY DECISION IS MADE AND WRITTEN DOWN in a comment at the offer site: goal-scoped with the environment in the payload, or one offer per environment. The payload keys are ["environment","network","sshTarget","url"] and the durable target is keyed per (project, environment) - state which authority the offer carries and how the environment is determined at dispatch. A test asserts the decided shape.

THE WITHHOLDING RULE IS STATED AND ASSERTED, and it is NOT the deploy offer's rule inverted carelessly: an operator needs set_target precisely when nothing is bound, and REBINDING an already-bound environment is legitimate. Say what withholds the offer, if anything, and assert both the offered and withheld cases as an offered-kind SET.

Every asserting consumer of the affordance surface is censused WHOLE-TREE and named with a verdict. `git grep -ln "affordance|nextAllowed|offered" -- 'tests/**'` returned 33 files at filing (tests/e2e, tests/integration, tests/security, tests/fault) plus four affordance test files under apps/daemon/src/http - all invisible to a package-scoped grep. Say which needed an arm and why the others did not.

MUTATION DRILL, quoted with its failing line: target the offer at the project aggregate instead of the decided key and confirm the by-value arm goes RED. Restore per global rail 13 - back the path up out of tree, restore from the backup rather than `git checkout --`, prove by sha256 in a separate call.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file; if the census found asserting consumers under tests/**, say which lanes you ran (`pnpm test:e2e`, `pnpm test:integration`) and which you did not.
taskRails: THE OFFER IS THE MISSING PIECE, NOT THE BUTTON. goal-deployments.tsx:189-192 correctly refuses to render a control with no affordance to spend; producing the offer is what unblocks it.
FOLLOW task-2cedb26a's PLAN - same emission site, same fallthrough, same by-value assertion discipline. A second pattern for the same problem is a second thing to reason about.
STATE THE GRANULARITY, DO NOT LEAVE IT TO THE BROWSER. Binding is per (project, environment); decide what the offer carries and write it at the offer site.
REBINDING IS LEGITIMATE. Do not withhold the offer merely because a target is already bound.
CENSUS THE WHOLE TREE, not just apps/daemon - 33 files under tests/** assert on this surface and none is visible to a package-scoped grep.
DO NOT CHANGE HOW set_target EXECUTES (task-358b6ec8) OR BUILD THE CONTROL (parent task-84cd2e55).

implementationPlan.description: MEASURE, AND CORRECT THE ROW'S PREMISE. NO EDITS. (a) `sed -n '30,55p' apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-contracts.ts` — confirm `deployment.set_target` is ALREADY on BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS (:51). (b) `sed -n '278,290p' apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts` — confirm the exclusion list is only `plan.propose`, `approval.decide`, `goal.close`, `repository.publish`, so an offer for set_target IS already pushed today. Together these mean THIS ROW RE-TARGETS AN EXISTING OFFER, it does not add one; say so in the step note, because the title and description both read as though none exists. (c) `sed -n '143,156p' apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts` — confirm `bootstrapAggregateId` special-cases only those four planning kinds and otherwise falls through to `aggregateIdFor`, i.e. the offer is currently PROJECT-targeted. (d) THE DEFECT THIS ROW REALLY FIXES: `sed -n '260,272p' apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts` — confirm that when `ledger.kinds.has(kind)` the loop returns COMMITTED and pushes NO offer, with a single hand-written exception for `policy.install` because it is repeatable. Confirm there is no such exception for `deployment.set_target`, which means the offer VANISHES after the first successful bind — directly contradicting task rail 4. (e) READ THE SIBLING'S DELIVERED DIFF: task-2cedb26a is landing the `aggregateIdFor` deployment case in bootstrap-sequence.ts. If its case already covers `deployment.set_target`, this row needs NO bootstrap-sequence.ts edit — record which it is, because that decides your file roster. (f) `grep -n "deployment" apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-payload-keys.ts` — confirm set_target's keys are `["environment","network","sshTarget","url"]`, which settles DoD 2. Record the global-rail-3 baseline for `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm typecheck`.

THE WHOLE-TREE CONSUMER CENSUS (DoD 4), BEFORE any edit — because it decides whether this plan's file roster is complete, and a consumer discovered at step 5 is a mid-flight surprise the rails forbid. Run `git grep -ln "affordance\|nextAllowed\|offered" -- 'tests/**'` and the same over `apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-*.test.ts` and `apps/control-room/src`. The DoD records 33 files under tests/** at filing (tests/e2e, tests/integration, tests/security, tests/fault) plus four affordance test files under apps/daemon/src/http — NONE of which is visible to a package-scoped grep or to `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`. For EACH hit, decide and record a verdict: does it pin an OFFERED SET by exact membership, a COUNT, or an exact `targetAggregateId`? Those are the ones that red when the id changes or when a second (repeat) offer appears. A test asserting a SUBSET will not. IF ANY CONSUMER NEEDS AN ARM OR AN UPDATE, it must be in this plan's affectedFiles — if the list exceeds what is planned here, STOP and report so the plan can be amended rather than discovering it at step 5 (global rail 19). "It did not need one" without a reason is not a verdict; say why.

RE-TARGET THE OFFER AND MAKE IT REPEATABLE — the two production changes, both in apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts (497 lines, already past the cap: add only these, do not refactor, several rows are editing it). (1) TARGET: give `deployment.set_target` the goal-scoped aggregate id the consuming control will match. Use the SAME key task-2cedb26a landed for the deployment family — read it from the delivered tree rather than re-deriving it, and if its `aggregateIdFor` case already covers set_target, take it for free and add nothing. Build the string with no separator drift; the card fences on the exact work-item key and an id that merely looks right renders nothing. (2) REPEATABILITY, the defect from step 1(d): add `deployment.set_target` to the after-commit offer exception beside `policy.install` at :263-270, so a committed binding STILL offers the next one. Pass `versionOf(ledger, aggregateId)` exactly as `policy.install` does — NOT 0 — so a rebind carries the aggregate's current version and the setter's CAS fence works. Without this the offer disappears the moment the first target is bound, which is precisely what task rail 4 forbids. (3) THE COMMENT DoD 2 REQUIRES, at the offer site, stating the decision AND its evidence: the offer is ONE per goal, not one per environment; the ENVIRONMENT TRAVELS IN THE PAYLOAD because daemon-command-payload-keys.ts:172 declares `["environment","network","sshTarget","url"]`, so a per-environment offer would put the environment in two places that can disagree; the durable target is keyed `deploy-target:<projectId>:<environment>` and that is the WRITE aggregate, NOT this work-item key; and NOTHING withholds this offer, because an operator needs it precisely when nothing is bound and rebinding is legitimate.

THE PRODUCTION-SURFACE ARMS (DoD 1, 2, 3), in apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.test.ts. ASSERT AGAINST THE PRODUCTION SURFACE READ, never a hand-built frame — a frame you construct proves the matcher string, not that the surface emits it. FOUR ARMS: (a) BY VALUE (DoD 1): the offered set contains `deployment.set_target` with `targetAggregateId` EQUAL BY VALUE to the decided key. Compare against the exact string, do not regex it. (b) NOT WITHHELD IN EITHER DIRECTION (DoD 3, and the inverse of the deploy offer): assert the offer is present when NO target is bound AND when one IS bound. Assert the offered-kind SET both times, not `toContain` — a subset assertion passes if the surface emitted a differently-named deployment offer instead. (c) REBINDING SURVIVES A COMMIT — the arm that pins step 3(2): drive a real `deployment.set_target` commit through the production path, read the surface AGAIN, and assert the offer is STILL there carrying the aggregate's CURRENT version, not 0. This is the arm that fails at HEAD today and the one that proves the repeatability fix; without it the row's central promise is untested. (d) GRANULARITY (DoD 2): with TWO environments bound, assert there is EXACTLY ONE set_target offer, not one per environment. That pins the decision so a later change cannot quietly switch axes.

MUTATION DRILLS (DoD 5), each restored and proved. `git status --porcelain` the exact mutated paths FIRST; these files are TRACKED, but DoD 5 asks for the stronger proof, so follow it: back the path up OUT OF TREE (%TEMP%, suffixed by your worker id), mutate, then restore FROM THE BACKUP rather than `git checkout --`, and prove by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore (global rail 13). TWO DRILLS: (i) THE ONE DoD 5 NAMES — target the offer at the PROJECT aggregate instead of the decided key (i.e. restore the fallthrough) and confirm the by-value arm from step 4(a) goes RED. QUOTE THE FAILING LINE. That failing line is the defect exactly as it exists at HEAD today: the surface believes it offered something and no control can match it. (ii) THE REPEATABILITY DRILL — remove `deployment.set_target` from the after-commit exception you added at :263-270 and confirm step 4(c) goes RED on the offer being ABSENT after the first bind. If it stays green, arm (c) is not actually reading the surface a second time and must be rewritten before you accept it; a rebinding rule that has never been seen red is not evidence, and this is the one that keeps the operator able to re-point a target.

GATES AND SELF-REVIEW (DoD 6). GATES — standalone and foreground, one command per call, no pipes and no `;` chains (a pipe reports tail's exit code; a chain reports only the last command's): `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm typecheck`, each quoted with its `Test Files N passed` count line; an exit-0 leg with NO count line RAN NOTHING (global rail 8), and `tsc` emits no count line by construction so say that rather than inventing one. Root `pnpm test` covers no `apps/**` file — say so rather than quoting it as evidence. IF STEP 2's CENSUS FOUND ASSERTING CONSUMERS UNDER `tests/**`, NEITHER LEG COVERS THEM: `tests/e2e` runs under `pnpm test:e2e` / `pnpm test:e2e:browser` and `tests/integration` under `pnpm test:integration`. Say which you ran and which you did not, and why — an untested consumer you knew about is worse than one you missed. If the exclusive full-suite lease is contended, cite a named recent full daemon run (holder, task, timestamps, HEAD sha, count line) and state whether it contains your landed bytes, rather than queueing. Attribute red by HEAD minus step 1's baseline, intersected with this row's owned paths. SELF-REVIEW: is the emitted id byte-identical to what the consuming control will match — no trailing separator, no project prefix; with two environments bound is there exactly ONE offer; does the generic loop still emit a stale PROJECT-targeted set_target offer alongside the goal-scoped one (if so the card may match the wrong one, and you must say which wins); and did you accidentally make any OTHER committed kind repeatable by widening the `policy.install` condition too far?

COMPLETION RECORD. Load `adversarial-self-review` and read your diff as an attacker first. THE RECORD MUST STATE: (1) THE PREMISE CORRECTION — that `deployment.set_target` was ALREADY offered at HEAD via BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS (bootstrap-contracts.ts:51) and the generic emission, targeted at the PROJECT, so this row RE-TARGETED an existing offer rather than adding one. The next reader will otherwise trust the row title. (2) THE REPEATABILITY DEFECT AND ITS FIX — that at HEAD the offer vanished after the first successful bind because only `policy.install` survived the `ledger.kinds.has(kind)` branch, that this made task rail 4's "rebinding is legitimate" unsatisfiable, and that the fix is the same exception shape carrying `versionOf(...)` so the setter's CAS fence still works. Name it as a defect found in planning, not as a design choice. (3) THE GRANULARITY DECISION with its evidence: ONE goal-scoped offer, environment in the payload, because payload-keys.ts:172 already carries it and a per-environment offer would let two sources disagree. (4) THE WITHHOLDING RULE: NOTHING withholds it — stated plainly, since it is the inverse of the deploy offer's rule and a later reader will expect symmetry. (5) The DoD-4 census verdict per file, naming which lanes you ran. (6) Both drill outcomes with their failing lines and sha256 restore proofs. (7) Whether task-2cedb26a's `aggregateIdFor` case covered set_target for free or you extended it — the next row in this family needs to know. Report every path in complete_step.modifiedFiles. Named verification command: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
THE ROW'S TITLE IS SLIGHTLY WRONG, AND THE CORRECTION CHANGES THE WORK. "The affordance surface offers deployment.set_target" reads as though no offer exists. It does. `deployment.set_target` is on BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS (bootstrap-contracts.ts:51) and is NOT in the four-name exclusion at affordance-read.ts:282-284 (`plan.propose`, `approval.decide`, `goal.close`, `repository.publish`), so the generic loop already pushes an offer for it — targeted at the PROJECT via the `bootstrapAggregateId` fallthrough (:143-155, which only special-cases the four planning kinds and otherwise defers to `aggregateIdFor`). The card's own comment is about the CONTROL having nothing to spend, which is true for a different reason: the offer is aimed at an aggregate no goal-scoped control matches. So this row RE-TARGETS an existing offer and makes it repeatable. It does not add one.

THE REPEATABILITY DEFECT, which is the substantive find and is in neither the description nor the DoD. affordance-read.ts:263-270: once a kind is present in the ledger the loop returns COMMITTED and pushes NO offer — with ONE hand-written exception for `policy.install`, which is special-cased precisely because it is repeatable. `deployment.set_target` is repeatable for the same reason (task rail 4: rebinding is legitimate), so at HEAD the offer DISAPPEARS the moment the first target is bound. That is the exact opposite of what an operator needs and it makes DoD 3's "rebinding is legitimate" unsatisfiable without this change. Fixing it is the same one-line shape `policy.install` already uses.

GRANULARITY — decided, and it matches the sibling for a measured reason, not for symmetry. `deployment.set_target`'s payload keys are `["environment", "network", "sshTarget", "url"]` (daemon-command-payload-keys.ts:172), so the environment is a DISPATCH-TIME field exactly as it is for `deployment.deploy` (`["environment", "sha"]`, :173). One offer per environment would therefore put the environment in two places that can disagree — the sibling's reasoning, and it transfers unchanged. So: ONE goal-scoped offer, environment in the payload.

WITHHOLDING — decided: NOTHING withholds it, and that is the whole point of the clause. The deploy offer is withheld when no target is bound; set_target is what the operator needs precisely then, and rebinding an already-bound environment is legitimate. So it is offered in BOTH the bound and unbound cases. "Nothing withholds it" is a real answer to DoD 3 provided it is stated and asserted in both directions, which the plan requires.

WHY I DID NOT HARD-PIN THE TARGET STRING. task-2cedb26a is still WORKING and lands the `aggregateIdFor` deployment case that decides it. Pinning a literal here would either duplicate its edit or collide with it. The plan instructs reading the delivered tree and reusing whatever key it landed — dependsOn already sequences the two.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD, 2026-09-06 (global rail 6). The description's central claim needs correcting; everything else it says checks out.

THE OFFER ALREADY EXISTS — the correction that reshapes this row:
- `deployment.set_target` IS on BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS, bootstrap-contracts.ts:51, appended with the comment "an ordinary synchronous write".
- It is NOT in ASYNC_SERVED_BOOTSTRAP_KINDS (:65-71) — that list holds `repository.bootstrap` and `deployment.deploy` only, and its comment says set_target "writes one durable binding and is a `BOOTSTRAP_HANDLERS` row like every other synchronous kind".
- The generic emission at affordance-read.ts:282-284 excludes only `plan.propose`, `approval.decide`, `goal.close`, `repository.publish`. set_target is none of those, so an offer IS pushed today.
- `bootstrapAggregateId` (affordance-read.ts:143-155) special-cases only those same four planning kinds against `planningSubject`, then falls through to `aggregateIdFor({kind, projectId}, DEFAULT_SUBJECTS[kind] ?? null)`. No deployment case exists yet — task-2cedb26a's step 2 is adding one.

THE REPEATABILITY DEFECT, affordance-read.ts:263-270 — read this block before editing:
```
if (ledger.kinds.has(kind)) {
  if (kind === "policy.install") {
    offers.push(offer(kind, aggregateId, versionOf(ledger, aggregateId), BOOTSTRAP_SCHEMA_VERSION));
  }
  return Object.freeze({ ... status: "COMMITTED" ... });
}
```
Only `policy.install` keeps offering after commit. So the FIRST successful `deployment.set_target` silently removes the offer, and the operator cannot rebind from the browser — directly contradicting task rail 4. This is the row's real defect and neither the description nor the DoD names it.

PAYLOAD KEYS, which settle DoD 2: daemon-command-payload-keys.ts:172 `"deployment.set_target": ["environment", "network", "sshTarget", "url"]`; :173 `"deployment.deploy": ["environment", "sha"]`. Environment is dispatch-time for BOTH.

THE DURABLE TARGET is keyed `deploy-target:<projectId>:<environment>` (deploy-target-contracts.ts:83-84). Note this is the WRITE aggregate, NOT the offer's work-item key — do not conflate them; the sibling's `deploy:<goalId>` is likewise not the deploy write aggregate.

THE CARD, goal-deployments.tsx:187-194: renders a kicker under `view.code === "DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING"` whose comment reads "no set_target affordance is offered, so a control here would have none to spend". There is NO set_target matcher yet — the control is task-4d77ba04's, and it will match on `commandKind === "deployment.set_target"` plus the target id this row emits.

THE SIBLING'S PLAN (task-2cedb26a, WORKING, 7 steps, unstarted at my read) is the pattern rail 2 binds me to: step 2 adds the deployment case to `aggregateIdFor` in bootstrap-sequence.ts returning `deploy:<goalId>` following the `repository.publish` case at :163; step 4 asserts BY VALUE against the production surface read, never a hand-built frame; step 5 is the whole-tree consumer census. Read its landed diff before editing — if its `aggregateIdFor` case covers BOTH deployment kinds, this row needs no bootstrap-sequence.ts edit at all.

planningNotes.risks:
1. THE REPEATABILITY CASE IS THE ROW. If you only re-target the offer and skip affordance-read.ts:263-270, the offer still vanishes after the first bind and task rail 4 is violated while every by-value arm passes. Assert the SECOND offer explicitly — bind once, read again, and require the offer to still be there.
2. DO NOT DUPLICATE OR COLLIDE WITH task-2cedb26a. It is landing the `aggregateIdFor` deployment case. Read the delivered tree first: if its case already covers `deployment.set_target`, do NOT add a second case, and say so. dependsOn sequences the two edits to affordance-planning-offers.ts / bootstrap-sequence.ts for exactly this reason.
3. affordance-read.ts IS 497 LINES, past the cap. Add the case and the comment only. Splitting it is not this row's job and would collide with several rows.
4. THE OFFER'S TARGET ID IS NOT THE DURABLE WRITE AGGREGATE. `deploy-target:<projectId>:<environment>` is where the setter WRITES; the offer carries a work-item key the card matches. Conflating them produces an id no control matches and no test catches unless the arm is by-value.
5. A SET ASSERTION, NOT A SUBSET (DoD 3 says so). `not.toContain` alone passes if the surface emitted a differently-named deployment offer. Assert the offered-kind SET in both the bound and unbound cases.
6. THE WHOLE-TREE CENSUS IS THE EASY MISS (DoD 4, task rail 5). 33 files under tests/** assert on this surface and NONE is visible to a package-scoped grep or to `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`. Any that pins an offered set by exact membership will red when the target id changes or a repeat offer appears — find them before the gate does, and say which lanes you ran.
7. REBINDING MUST NOT BE CONFUSED WITH REPLAY. The setter is replace-not-duplicate with a CAS fence (task-358b6ec8's reviewSummary). The offer must carry the aggregate's CURRENT version so a rebind fences correctly — `policy.install` already shows the shape, passing `versionOf(ledger, aggregateId)` rather than 0.
